Although other sampling strategies exist, local schemes have become standard: such schemes map each k -mer to the position of one of its characters. A key performance measure of these schemes is their density, defined as the expected fraction of selected positions. The most widely used local scheme is the minimizer scheme: given an integer m ≤ k , a minimizer scheme associates each k -mer to the starting position of one of its m -mers, called its minimizer . Being a local scheme, the minimizer scheme guarantees covering all k -mers of a sequence, with a maximal distance between selected positions of w = k − m + 1. Recent works have established near-tight lower bounds on achievable density under standard assumptions for local schemes, and state-of-the-art schemes now operate close to these limits, suggesting that further improvements under the classical notion of density will face diminishing returns. Hence, in this work, we aim to revisit the notion of density and broaden its scope. As a first contribution, we draw a link between density and the distance between consecutive selected positions. We propose a probabilistic model allowing us to establish that the density of a local scheme is exactly the inverse of the expected distance between the positions it selects, under the minimal and only assumption that said distances are somehow equally distributed. We emphasize here that our model makes no assumptions about how positions are selected, unlike the classical models in the literature. Our result introduces a novel method for computing the density of a local scheme, extending beyond classical settings. Based on this analysis, we introduce a novel technique, named multiminimizers, by associating each k -mer with a bounded set of candidate minimizers rather than a single one. The candidate furthest away (in a precise sense defined in the article) is selected. We show that this method, when applied to random (hash-based) minimizers and to open-closed mod-minimizers, approaches a density of , representing, to our knowledge, the first construction converging to this limit. title: Quartic Certificates for Pure-State Tomography with Pauli Measurements
abstract: Full Pauli-basis tomography of an arbitrary $n$-qubit state uses the expectation values of all nonidentity Pauli observables. For multiqubit systems, prior knowledge that the state is pure allows some of these observables to be omitted while retaining uniqueness. We study two resulting notions of uniqueness: whether every pure state is uniquely determined among pure states (UDP), and whether every pure state is uniquely determined among all states, including mixed states (UDA). We derive quartic uniqueness certificates from the fourth elementary symmetric polynomial of operators in the real span of the omitted Pauli observables. An exact quartic identity shows that, for $n$-qubit systems with $n\geq 3$, every pure state is UDA whenever the omitted Pauli observables contain no four distinct operators that commute pairwise and multiply to $\pm I$. For three qubits, this condition is also necessary for UDP, yielding an exact characterization of both UDP and UDA. We further prove that UDP and UDA coincide for any number of qubits whenever the omitted Pauli observables commute pairwise. These results provide directly checkable structural criteria for certifying pure-state tomography from restricted Pauli measurements.

title: Syn-Omni: Structured Specialization and Progressive Collaboration for Omnimodal Embeddings
abstract: Omnimodal embeddings naturally involve both shared representations and modality-specific features across heterogeneous inputs. However, existing omnimodal embedding methods often rely on a single shared parameter space over mixed-modality data, limiting structural separation between universal and modality-specific representations. To address this, we propose Syn-Omni, a unified framework for structured omnimodal adaptation with modality specialization and controlled cross-modal collaboration. Specifically, we introduce Orthogonal Modality-Expert LoRA (OME-LoRA), which decomposes adaptation into a shared LoRA path for universal semantics and modality-expert LoRA paths for modality-aware specialization. Furthermore, Progressive Synergy Routing (PSR) enables experts to first establish modality-specific priors, then gradually interact with other modality-experts for cross-modal synergy. Evaluated across 81 diverse tasks spanning image, video, audio, and audiovisual modalities, Syn-Omni consistently outperforms omnimodal baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness of structured specialization and cross-modal progressive collaboration.

title: Example-driven Parametrisations for Bayesian Shape Optimisation
abstract: Bayesian optimisation is the natural tool for shape design when objectives are expensive and non-differentiable, but it needs a compact yet expressive parameterisation of the search space. Hand-crafting one is a complex endeavour requiring domain expertise, and often yields implicit infeasible regions, artificial bounds, and coupled, unordered coordinates. We instead learn the parameterisation from a collection of existing designs, applying principal component analysis to the deformations between shapes. The result is a linear, interpretable search space in which the number of components explicitly trades expressivity against dimensionality. Across aerofoils, wings, and radio-frequency cavities, spanning 2D geometry to 3D aerodynamics and electromagnetics, we show improved sample efficiency and the ability to explore beyond the confines of hand-crafted baselines.

title: Conditional Residual Prediction: Improving Autoregressive Video Diffusion without a Bidirectional Teacher
abstract: Causal video diffusion models generate video autoregressively, which suits streaming, interactive, and long-video generation. Under standard training, however, they often yield lower generation quality than bidirectional models of the same size. Many existing approaches address this gap by initializing from or distilling a pretrained bidirectional teacher. We instead train a causal model from an image-model initialization, with no bidirectional video model at any stage. Because this path requires neither a large bidirectional teacher nor a complex distillation pipeline, it is simpler and more scalable. On this path, we find that a causal model trained on ground-truth history becomes strongly dependent on it, so that at inference errors in its own generated history propagate forward. We hypothesize that much of this dependence is unnecessary, because the current input already determines much of what the history provides. We propose Conditional Residual Prediction (CRP), a simple recipe for reducing a model's reliance on a condition: the model first predicts the target without the condition, and the condition may only add a residual on top of this prediction. Applied to history, CRP makes the model predict each chunk from the present as far as it can and use the past only for what the present cannot supply. In controlled experiments, CRP nearly closes the 6.14-point gap to a bidirectional model trained under the same setup. Scaling this recipe, we train Optica, a 2B-parameter causal video model that autoregressively generates 5-second 480p videos and reaches 82.78 on VBench with only about 15M training videos.

title: Gap Sensitivity and Bottleneck Migration in Sparse Constraint-Preserving Quantum Annealing
abstract: Constraint-preserving exchange drivers allow many coupling graphs that preserve the same feasible sector, but exhibit different minimum gaps along an annealing path. We derive an exchange-resolved sensitivity of the normalised minimum gap for fixed-cardinality Laplacian drivers sharing a Dicke ground state, and apply it to identify locally favourable modifications of the driver. Numerical experiments indicate this sensitivity reliably predicts beneficial infinitesimal changes, but its reliability decreases when the same direction is extended to a finite edge replacement. The gap landscape tracking reveals one mechanism of this loss of reliability. Improving the active bottleneck can expose a competing minimum, with a more extensive reorganisation of the low-energy subspace. We call this the "repair-and-expose" mechanism and observe it in both dense quadratic and sparse frustrated objective families. This motivates relinearizing the response when competing minima become co-active. In the tested oracle setting, a tied-minimum max-min update is substantially more reliable than continuing the original direction or optimizing only the incoming minimum. Supporting finite-size search and selector tests show that this local information can remain useful beyond the infinitesimal limit, while its practical extraction depends on the driver geometry and identification of the relevant low-energy competitors. These results connect local exchange-resolved gap sensitivity to bottleneck migration and conditional driver redirection.

title: Refine Connections, Close the Gap: A Reliable Enhancement Framework for Driving Scene Topology
abstract: In autonomous driving, understanding scene topology - the connectivity between lanes and traffic elements - is critical for safe path planning and motion control. While current methods excel at detecting individual map elements, their connectivity reasoning often falls short of its theoretical potential, leaving a significant performance gap relative to the theoretical upper-bound achievable given the underlying detections. Furthermore, the decision-ready topology graphs passed to downstream tasks often remain unreliable. Current approaches typically derive connectivity by thresholding continuous topology scores; however, these scores often fail to reflect the true logical likelihood of connectivity, resulting in false positives or missing connections. Existing benchmarks further overlook this issue by primarily evaluating continuous metrics, rather than assessing the discrete connectivity required for decision-making. To bridge these gaps, we propose TopoEnhance, a novel topology enhancement framework designed to unlock the latent potential of existing methods and improve the reliability of decision-ready topology. We formulate topology enhancement as a denoising-based reconstruction process, where the model learns to recover structural consistency from stochastically corrupted ground-truth graphs. This formulation enables the model to resolve logical inconsistencies and rectify unreliable connections, producing robust discrete topology graphs that closely approach theoretical maximum performance. Extensive experiments across different baselines show that TopoEnhance consistently improves both continuous topology metrics (TOP score), and discrete connectivity measured by our adapted Topology Jaccard Similarity (TJS) metric. As a flexible, source-agnostic framework, TopoEnhance delivers substantial gains across diverse state-of-the-art baselines without requiring retraining.

title: Evaluation of synthetic data generation for longitudinal 6-year follow-up subclinical cardiovascular disease data using GAN models
abstract: Abstract Although largely preventable, cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide. Synthetic data generation (SDG) of health data can facilitate data sharing for research and development of personalised cardiovascular disease prevention tools. Current state-of-the-art SDG methods are limited to cross-sectional data or focused on short-term or in-patient EHR applications lacking benchmarks for generalisability. Since prevention is a long-term longitudinal objective, these limitations must be addressed. We evaluated two tabular generative adversarial networks, TGAN and CTGAN, for privacy and fidelity on a structured 6-year longitudinal trial dataset within CVD prevention. We compared performance with a rudimentary perturbation method. In addition, we performed a variable-wise evaluation and an age-stratified analysis of the higher performing model to assess preservation of clinically relevant characteristics. Overall, CTGAN showed better fidelity than TGAN. The models performed similarly within privacy, showing better results than the perturbation method. CTGAN had lower performance in comparison to the perturbation method within numerical fidelity of continuous variables and overall temporal fidelity. Furthermore, CTGAN’s performance was lower for younger age groups than older. CTGAN shows better than or equal performance within fidelity and privacy than TGAN and the perturbation method on a long-term longitudinal dataset within CVD prevention. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study evaluating CTGAN on a longitudinal dataset and our findings suggest that handling of temporal characteristics and imbalanced subgroups need further refinement.

title: Evolución del Marketing Impulsado por Inteligencia Artificial en el Ecosistema Emprendedor Ecuatoriano: Una Revisión Sistemática a Partir del COVID-19
abstract: This study aimed to analyze the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven marketing within the Ecuadorian entrepreneurial ecosystem since the COVID-19 pandemic. A systematic literature review was conducted using a qualitative approach, with a descriptive scope and a non-experimental design. Study selection followed the PRISMA 2020 statement, drawing on scientific databases such as Scopus, Web of Science, SciELO, ScienceDirect, Dialnet, and ResearchGate, and was limited to studies published between 2020 and 2026 in Spanish and English. Of the 398 records identified, 32 studies were included after screening and eligibility assessment and were analyzed chronologically. The results reveal a gradual trajectory: between 2020 and 2022, ventures shifted their activities to basic digital channels in order to survive; in 2023, AI began to be incorporated to process information and automate campaigns; in 2024, its adoption expanded into customer service through chatbots and personalized offers; and between 2025 and 2026, its generative use became consolidated for creating content and advertising materials. It is concluded that AI has already become part of marketing in Ecuadorian ventures, as it has been progressively integrated into their commercial processes.

title: Theory of Everything Research Programme: Block III Retention, Feedback and Learning Confirmatory Experiment Software and Reproducibility Package.
abstract: This software release provides the executable and reproducibility infrastructure for the preregistered confirmatory study in Experimental Block III of the Theory of Everything Research Programme. The package implements the frozen protocol associated with OSF preregistration DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/8ZWM7. It contains seven frozen confirmatory manifests and integrity locks, twenty held-out seeds, confirmatory-only task variants, explicit implementations of policy-accessible retained state, within-episode closed-loop feedback and between-episode learning, serious bypass architectures, retained-state interventions, feedback delays and channel perturbations, learning-update ablations, full factorial R × F × L analysis, provenance capture, automated decision logic and reproducibility tests. The confirmatory study returned RETAIN for H3.1 through H3.7. The overall mechanism-level decisions were RETAIN for retention, feedback, learning and mechanism separability. The registered bypasses also succeeded where expected: direct present-state augmentation bypassed online retention, matched open-loop control handled predictable disturbance, and explicit mapping context bypassed parameter learning. These results support the mechanisms as causally useful under the registered task requirements while arguing against universal necessity claims. This release is paired with the Block III confirmatory dataset and decision record (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23244857) and implements the experimental methodology described in Working Paper III (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22857230). The scope is deliberately limited. The study does not establish general intelligence, explicit world modelling, counterfactual planning, reflective self-awareness or phenomenal consciousness.

title: Socratic guiding questions in synthetic arithmetic data: matched LoRA runs (revision v2)
abstract: Supporting data, adapters, predictions and code for the article *Low-Cost LoRA Fine-Tuning of Small Language Models for Multi-Step Arithmetic Reasoning* by Jake O'Grady, Asena Isik Gürhan, Chee Fong Ting and Effirul Ramlan (University of Galway). We generated 20,000 GSM8K-derived arithmetic problems with step-by-step solutions and rendered each solution twice: with a guiding question before every reasoning step (Socratic) and without those questions (non-Socratic). Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-1.7B and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct were fine-tuned with LoRA on both versions, and Qwen3-0.6B also on nested subsets of 5,000 and 10,000 examples. All models were evaluated on GSM8K, MultiArith, SVAMP and GSM-Hard under a protocol fixed before any run.See README.md for the file list, licences and how to verify every number.

title: AI-DRIVEN ADVANCES IN CANCER DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT
abstract: Cancer is one of the most significant concerns of the health system in the world and early diagnosis and personalised treatment will be significant drivers in improving the outcome of patients. Cancer prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment and monitoring are today an exciting area of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for cancer. Using AI, machine learning, deep learning and natural language processing (NLP) have the potential to capture tremendous amounts of information from clinical and imaging data, pathology, the genomic and molecular data. AI analysis of the CT, MRI, PET and histopathological images can aid in early diagnosis and the detection and classification of tumours. Precise oncology uses AI to integrate genomic information and clinical data and make precise, personalized treatment choices, patient categorization, prognosis of how patients will respond to treatment and predict whether they will return. AI is also playing a role in anticancer drug discovery in repurposing drugs, prediction of drug-target interaction and optimization of drug candidates. However, there are issues like robustness of data, privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, clinical validation and regulatory issues that need to be addressed. In total, the possibilities for AI to enhance the accuracy, efficiency, individualisation and patient-centredness of cancer treatment and care are huge.

title: PROBLEMS OF FORMING A LINGUISTIC BASE WHEN CREATING A CORPUS
abstract: The development of a linguistic foundation for corpus construction poses a number of important difficulties that may have an impact on the final dataset's quality and usability. The ambiguity in defining the corpus's scope and purpose is one of the main problems, which might cause the texts chosen to be out of alignment. This could lead to a corpus that is not representative enough to capture the variety of language use across various groups and circumstances.384 Another difficulty is gathering data, especially when it comes to accessibility and copyright limitations that restrict the variety of texts that can be included. Additionally, if the corpus is unduly concentrated on particular genres or linguistic variants while ignoring others, sampling bias may result.

abstract: Сунъий интеллект технологияларининг жадал ривожланиши замонавий жамиятни ўзгартиришнинг энг муҳим омилларидан бирига айланмоқда. title: Early epilepsy detection from electronic health records with large language models
abstract: Epilepsy and psychogenic non-epileptic seizures often present with similar seizure-like manifestations but require fundamentally different management strategies. Misdiagnosis is common and can lead to prolonged diagnostic delays, unnecessary treatments, and substantial patient morbidity. Although prolonged video-electroencephalography is the diagnostic gold standard, its high cost and limited accessibility hinder timely diagnosis. Here, we developed a low-cost, effective approach, EpiScreen, for early epilepsy detection by utilizing routinely collected clinical notes from electronic health records. Through fine-tuning large language models on labeled notes, EpiScreen achieved an AUC of up to 0.875 on the MIMIC-IV dataset and 0.980 on a private cohort of the University of Minnesota. In a clinician-AI collaboration setting, EpiScreen-assisted neurologists outperformed unaided experts by up to 14.3%. Overall, this study demonstrates that EpiScreen supports early epilepsy detection, facilitating timely and cost-effective screening that may reduce diagnostic delays and avoid unnecessary interventions, particularly in resource-limited regions.

title: MIRAGE: Metric Inference and Reliability-Aware Gaussian Estimation from Feed-Forward Vision
abstract: Feed-forward 3D priors enable high-quality reconstruction from image streams but often lack reliable metric scale and suffer from long-term trajectory drift. In contrast, LiDAR--inertial estimation provides metrically accurate motion but lacks the image-space consistency needed for high-fidelity reconstruction. We propose $MIRAGE$, which anchors feed-forward visual geometry to LiDAR--IMU metric motion and regulates online pose corrections according to correspondence support and cross-modal agreement, jointly enabling accurate metric pose estimation and high-fidelity Gaussian reconstruction. Experiments on Oxford Spires, M2DGR and INS show that MIRAGE achieves accurate metric trajectory estimation, outperforming COLMAP, a widely used but computationally expensive reference for vision-only benchmarks. Motivated by the scarcity of long-horizon monocular benchmarks for large-scale indoor reconstruction, we further build a multimodal data-collection platform and use MIRAGE to establish accurate 6-DoF reference trajectories for a new vision-only benchmark. We benchmark recent monocular large-scale reconstruction methods on this dataset, providing a systematic evaluation of their performance in long-horizon indoor scenes.

title: Scalable LEO Conjunction Screening using Adaptive Synthetic-Covariance Thresholds
abstract: As orbital populations grow, conjunction screening must search more object pairs for potential collision risks. Existing pipelines use early-stage filters, such as an apsis filter, to eliminate pairs whose orbital altitude ranges cannot produce a close approach. However, these filters apply the same fixed threshold to every object, making the screening unnecessarily conservative for well-constrained objects while potentially insufficient for objects with greater orbit-prediction uncertainty. In this work, we present an uncertainty-aware conjunction screening method that replaces a single fixed apsis threshold with object-specific thresholds derived from propagated radial uncertainty. The resulting thresholds vary across both objects and prediction time, becoming narrower when propagated uncertainty is small and wider when uncertainty grows. We pair this adaptive screening rule with a binary-search altitude sweep that makes resulting heterogeneous intervals efficient to evaluate at catalog scale with log-linear search complexity. We evaluate the method on 33,791 objects from the Space-Track General Perturbations (GP) catalog using the preceding eight public ephemeris snapshots and a seven-day prediction horizon. The adaptive sieve retains 162.8 million candidate pairs, reducing the candidate set by 28.78% relative to a fixed 50 km apsis threshold and by 71.48% relative to brute-force all-pairs screening. It retains all close approaches identified in two independently propagated reference sets. At the largest tested catalog size, the binary-search sweep is 27 times faster than exhaustive interval evaluation while returning the same candidate set. These results demonstrate that uncertainty-aware screening can substantially reduce the candidate burden passed to downstream conjunction analysis, providing a scalable path toward managing increasingly large and heterogeneous orbital populations.

title: Asking Instead of Listening: A Semantic Voice Activity Detector for Turn Decisions
abstract: While acoustic Voice Activity Detection (VAD) determines the presence of speech, conversational voice pipelines require semantic decision-making to handle turn-taking dynamics. This paper introduces jev-vad, a lightweight, model-agnostic semantic VAD layer that replaces heuristic barge-in and end-of-turn predictions with typed questions evaluated by a small System-1 decision model. Instantiated via an int4-quantized ONNX export of Laya (a ~206 MB, CPU-only mmBERT-base encoder), jev-vad processes serialized dialogue state (the agent's prior utterance plus the partial transcript) in a single non-autoregressive forward pass to yield per-option choice probabilities. We demonstrate that barge-in and turn-end decisions possess opposing failure-cost asymmetries, requiring two separately tuned questions: barge-in detection requires recall-biased tuning (achieving an F1 score of 0.76 at a 0.30 threshold with a filler guard), whereas end-of-turn prediction demands precision-biased tuning combined with acoustic pause detection. Evaluated on a 100-phrase Spanish benchmark, we uncover a language-mixing phenomenon where English question framing over Spanish dialogue state yields up to a +0.40 accuracy improvement for barge-in detection, while turn-end detection requires native Spanish framing. The winning configuration runs in 101–187 ms p50 on an 8-vCPU cloud instance, providing a fully self-hosted solution alongside a reproducible ablation methodology for cross-lingual adaptation.

title: Developmental Analysis and Technical Report: Small Language Model (SLM) Training from Scratch
abstract: This report documents the ongoing development and empirical analysis of a 4.2-million-parameter Transformer-based small language model (SLM) trained from scratch by Novum Labs. The objective of this project is to evaluate the learning trajectory, convergence dynamics, semantic coherence, and dataset scaling characteristics of compact language models constrained by lightweight compute environments (CPU/local workstations). The report covers baseline training runs, loss optimization using Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE), text generation evaluation, and a strategic roadmap for future scaling.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Resource Allocation in Economics
abstract: This chapter investigates the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in improving resource allocation across business, economics, and finance. Traditional resource allocation methods, which rely heavily on historical data, manual analysis, and static planning models, increasingly struggle to respond effectively to dynamic and data-intensive environments. The chapter identifies major limitations of conventional allocation systems, including limited data-processing capabilities, inability to adapt to changing conditions, subjectivity and bias, inefficient resource utilisation, and weak risk management practices. It further explores how AI- and ML-driven technologies address these challenges through predictive analytics, automation, real-time decision-making, and intelligent forecasting. Key application areas discussed include demand forecasting, inventory management, production planning, financial resource allocation, supply chain management, human resource management, and workforce optimisation. Drawing on practical examples from leading global organisations, the chapter demonstrates that AI and ML enhance operational efficiency, improve strategic decision-making, reduce waste, and strengthen organisational competitiveness in increasingly complex economic environments.

title: ДОИР БА МАРҲИЛАҲОИ БАҚАЙДГИРИИ ДАВЛАТИИ ТАЪСИСЁБИИ ТАШКИЛОТҲОИ ҒАЙРИТИҶОРАТӢ ҲАМЧУН ШАХСИ ҲУҚУҚӢ ДАР ШАКЛИ ТАШКИЛДИҲӢ
abstract: Дар мақолаи мазкур муаллиф доир ба масъалаи марҳилаҳои бақайдгирии давлатии таъсисёбии ташкилотҳои ғайритиҷоратӣ ҳамчун шахси ҳуқуқӣ дар шакли ташкилдиҳӣ изҳори ақида менамояд. Мақсади таҳқиқоти мазкур пеш аз ҳама, таҳқиқ ва омӯзиши илмии падидаи марҳилаҳои бақайдгирии давлатии таъсисёбии ташкилотҳои ғайритиҷоратӣ дар шакли ташкилдиҳӣ дар Ҷумҳурии Тоҷикистон мебошад. Дар мақолаи мазкур пеш аз ҳама, сарчашмаҳои гуногуни марбут ба шаклҳои ташкилӣ-ҳуқуқӣ, навъҳо ва намудҳои ташкилотҳои ғайритиҷоратии Ҷумҳурии Тоҷикистон мавриди таҳлил қарор дода шудааст. Ҳамзамон, зимни таҳқии мавзуи таҳқиқи мазкур методҳои ҳуқуқии умумиилмӣ ва махсуси илмӣ мавриди истифода қарор дода шудаанд. Муаллиф, марҳилаҳои бақайдгирии давлатии таъсисёбии ташкилотҳои ғайритиҷоратӣ дар шакли ташкилдиҳиро аз нахуст, таҳия ва пешниҳоди ҳуҷҷатҳо барои бақайдгирии давлатӣ ба мақоми ваколатдори давлатӣ, дуюм, мақоми ваколатдори амалисозандаи бақайдгирии давлатӣ, сеюм, муҳлати бақайдгирии давлатӣ, чорум, рад намудани бақайдгирии давлатӣ ва шикоят намудан нисбати рад намудани бақайдгирии давлатӣ, панҷум, пешбурди феҳристи ягонаи давлатии шахсони ҳуқуқӣ, шашум, тартиби боздоштани фаъолияти шахсони ҳуқуқӣ иборат донистааст. Зимни таҳлили марҳилаҳои мазкур як қатор камбудиҳо ва норасоиҳо муайян ва баҳри ислоҳи онҳо таклифҳои дахлдор баён гардидааст. Дар охир муаллиф, чун қоида нисбати мавзуи таҳқиқи мазкур хулосаи дахлдор низ пешниҳод намудааст.

title: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings
abstract: Hierarchical text embedding models offer variable-length representations, while quantization reduces numerical precision; both aim to improve computational efficiency. This work is an empirical benchmark study of how these two orthogonal, already-established techniques interact. We evaluate 38 tasks from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) using four transformer-based embedding models, covering 1D and 2D hierarchical representations combined with 32-bit, 8-bit, and binary quantization, for 168 configurations per task. We report each efficiency dimension separately: theoretical per-vector storage and end-to-end evaluation time. Under a Friedman test with Nemenyi post-hoc analysis, int8 quantization is statistically indistinguishable from float32 for pair classification and re-ranking and costs at most 1.5 percentage points overall, whereas binary quantization is significantly worse across every task category. Halving the embedding dimension once is not statistically detectable above ; two successive halvings always are. Combining an 8 dimensionality reduction with int8 yields a 32 reduction in per-vector storage at 94.4% of baseline effectiveness. Because evaluation times were measured once, we treat them as indicative: we find no evidence that quantization speeds up evaluation, whereas sampling from intermediate layers shortens it substantially. Retrieval degrades far faster than every other category, so we report findings per task category.

title: Enabling Extended SGX Enclaves inside Confidential Virtual Machines
abstract: Confidential Virtual Machines (CVMs), such as AMD SEV-SNP, and process enclaves, such as Intel SGX, provide workload protection against cloud threats. However, they strongly differ in TCB, deployment cost and speed, peer workload protection, resource sharing, fine-grained isolation and attestation, and programming capabilities. Nesting process enclaves within CVMs offers an optimal solution and an opportunity to address long-standing SGX limitations: lack of intra-enclave protection, expensive transitions and exception paths, slow enclave cloning, and a restricted programming model that limits Library Operating Systems (LibOS). This paper introduces TEEVisor, a CVM-resident architecture consisting of a security monitor and a kernel driver that leverages AMD SEV-SNP Virtual Machine Privilege Levels (VMPLs) to build hardware-protected, process-level enclaves inside a guest CVM with two modes: (1) an SGX binary compatibility mode to run unmodified SGX applications; and (2) a novel extended SGX~(eSGX) mode optimizing slow execution paths and offering richer enclave programming capabilities. title: How Much Audio Is Left In An Embedding? An Inversion Audit Of Audio Encoders
abstract: Pretrained audio encoders are reused for downstream tasks that are often unknown when the encoder is trained, so their usefulness depends partly on which signal properties survive the pretext objective. We study this retained information through paired source reconstruction. Using a shared Stable Audio Open latent diffusion decoder, we reconstruct five-second, 44.1-kHz stereo music from frozen representations produced by supervised classifiers (VGGish, ConvNeXt), an audio-text contrastive model (CLAP), and a waveform-reconstruction model (EnCodec). These objectives impose different pressures to preserve source detail, while their exposed interfaces vary substantially in temporal and spectral resolution. Evaluating on the Million Song Dataset (MSD), we find clear differences in reconstructability across encoder families, while within encoder comparisons show improved recovery when finer temporal or spectral structure is exposed. Even compressed task oriented embeddings support reconstructions that preserve measurable source specificity and high level musical content.

title: Gravitational Microlensing
abstract: Gravitational microlensing is a unique planet-detection method that does not rely on detecting light from the host star or planet. Instead, planets are discovered when their gravitational field perturbs the light coming from a distant source. The mechanics of this method offer several advantages. It has the ability to detect wide-orbit planets of various masses around host stars of different types, at and beyond the system's snow line. Thus, microlensing complements the other detecting techniques that are more sensitive to close-orbit or high-mass planets. In this Chapter, we review the microlensing method and discuss how the physical properties, such as mass and distance, can be extracted from the microlensing light curve or from additional high-angular resolution observations. Microlensing is essential for the broader context of exoplanet demographics, as it can place constraints on planets, in wide orbits, beyond the {\it snow line}. Studying this parameter space can help us unravel the details of planet formation and how our own Solar System formed. Lastly, we provide an example of how to model a light curve and obtain accurate physical parameters for the host and planet.

title: Regularized Small Area Estimation with Graph Laplacian Benchmarking priors
abstract: Small area estimation (SAE) often requires both borrowing information across areas and benchmarking estimates to reliable aggregates. We develop a Bayesian framework that addresses these two objectives jointly through a new family of Benchmarking priors. The priors are induced by a benchmark-constrained regularization problem. The resulting family includes a Benchmarking Prior that incorporates the benchmarking restrictions without additional regularization across areas, and Single and Multi-View Laplacian Benchmarking Priors that introduce regularization through graph Laplacians constructed from area similarities based on external covariate information. For posterior computation under these degenerate priors, we develop tailored MCMC algorithms based on a reduced parameterization of the constraint space. We assess the proposed models using a data-based simulation and apply the framework to estimate Average Household Size (AHS) at the municipality level in Colombia in 2025. In this application, graph-based regularization improves model performance, with the Multi-View models generally producing more precise municipality-level estimates.

title: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis of Google Maps Reviews For Barbershop Competitor and Brand Strategy Analysis Using Machine Learning
abstract: Customer reviews on Google Maps contain information regarding service experiences but are unstructured and may discuss multiple aspects within a single review. This study applies Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) to analyze customer perceptions across 23 barbershops and compare the performance of Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, and IndoBERT. A total of 5,418 reviews were collected from the selected barbershops and processed through cleaning, preprocessing, aspect identification, and aspect-level lexicon-based sentiment labeling. After cleaning and deduplication, 5,299 reviews generated 7,457 aspect-level observations classified into positive, neutral, and negative sentiment. Naive Bayes, SVM, and Random Forest used TF-IDF representations, while IndoBERT used contextual transformer-based representations. Evaluation using accuracy, precision, recall, Macro F1-score, and ROC-AUC showed that IndoBERT achieved an accuracy of 98.57%, precision of 93.28%, recall of 93.99%, Macro F1-score of 93.55%, and ROC-AUC of 99.88%. General, Result Quality, and Service were the most frequently identified aspects, while Cleanliness, Comfort, and Service had the highest proportions of positive sentiment. Waiting Time and Price showed relatively higher proportions of negative sentiment. A Wilson Score Lower Bound was used as supplementary descriptive information for comparing the relative positions of the 23 barbershops. Because sentiment labels were automatically generated using a lexicon-based procedure, the classification and competitor-analysis results represent performance and descriptive patterns based on weak labels rather than manually annotated ground truth.

title: Quranic LLM Translation Evaluation_Gemini and DeepSeek
abstract: This dataset contains the Arabic source verses, English and French reference translations, machine-generated translations produced by Gemini and DeepSeek, and the corresponding automatic evaluation scores. The dataset comprises 514 Qur'anic verses and was prepared for a comparative evaluation of large language model-generated Qur'anic translations from Arabic into English and French. The evaluation uses COMET-22, which requires reference translations, and COMETKiwi, which evaluates translation quality without a reference translation.

title: A Unified Logical Framework for Faithful Explanations: Translation and Projection across Tree, Linear, and Neural Models — Reproducibility Artifact
abstract: Reproducibility artifact for the current manuscript prepared for Knowledge-Based Systems. Includes nine scripts, dataset metadata and split indices, dated protocols, and final reference results for independent tree-rule utility, cross-model comparisons, complete projections, matched path-subset controls, and GPU follow-up audits. The standard-library verifier checks 101 reference files. Experimental figures can be regenerated from the supplied tables. This updated artifact supersedes the experimental package in v1.0.0; the earlier release and DOI remain available as historical records. See README.md for installation, reproduction commands, and interpretation limits.

title: Code and data for "From annotation towards surveillance: adapted open-weight large language models for article-level 5C classification of vaccination-related media discourse, Slovenia, 2010–2024"
abstract: Code, prompts, codebook and de-identified result files for the article "From annotation towards surveillance: adapted open-weight large language models for article-level 5C classification of vaccination-related media discourse, Slovenia, 2010–2024" by Mario Fafangel, Janez Žibert and Lijana Zaletel-Kragelj (manuscript for Eurosurveillance). The study built a two-stage pipeline of open-weight large language models. A relevance classifier decides whether a mainstream-media article is about vaccination, and an extractor records which of the 5C constructs the article contains (Confidence, Complacency, Constraints, Calculation, Collective Responsibility) and the valence of each. Two model families, Qwen3-32B and Apertus-8B, were adapted with LoRA and one round of active learning and scored once on a held-out evaluation set of 100 double-annotated articles, on which the better-performing family was also chosen. The pipeline was then applied to the weeks around the September 2021 suspension of a COVID-19 vaccine in Slovenia. The labels describe how articles frame vaccination; they do not measure individual attitudes or behaviour. The record contains the annotation codebook, the two prompts, the adaptation and decoding settings, the pipeline source from sampling to inference, the analysis scripts, de-identified per-article result files for six systems, the weekly event-window series, the event-window audit labels and six invented example articles. The record also holds the two annotators' labels before adjudication, the predictions on the machine-translated English articles and two sampled-decoding runs of Apertus-8B, all without text, and the scripts used for the machine translation. Running python reproduce.py recomputes the evaluation-set, event-window, audit, inter-annotator, cross-lingual and decoding-check results and checks them against the values printed in the article and its supplement. The corpus, sampling, active-learning and candidate counts need the restricted corpus, and the two audit coders' separate codings are available from the authors on request. No article text is included. The corpus is an institutional press-clipping corpus held by the National Institute of Public Health Slovenia (NIJZ) and is subject to the terms of the press-clipping service. The four LoRA adapters reported in the article are on Hugging Face. Licences: MIT for code; CC BY 4.0 for documentation, codebook, prompts and data. The adapters carry the Apache-2.0 licence of their base models.
